'''Peter Shaw Ashton''' (born 27 June 1934)<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Peter Shaw Ashton Curriculum Vitae|url=http://www.huh.harvard.edu/ctfs/ctfs/pdf/PSA_CV.pdf|work=Center for Tropical Forest Science-Arnold Arboretum Asia Program|accessdate=25 April 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100627012847/http://www.huh.harvard.edu/ctfs/ctfs/pdf/PSA_CV.pdf|archivedate=27 June 2010}}</ref> is a British [[Botany|botanist]] and [[Forest ecology|forest ecologist]]. He worked as the Charles Bullard Professor of Forestry at [[Harvard University]] from 1991 to 2005 and served as director of the [[Arnold Arboretum]] from 1978 to 1987.

== Life and career ==
Born in [[Boscombe]], [[Bournemouth]], [[England]], Ashton received his B.A. in Biology (1956), M.A. in Biology (1960) and Ph.D. in Botany (1962) from the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="CV" /> He has worked for many years on research projects to promote the conservation and sustainable use of tropical forests, and was instrumental in the project by the [[Center for Tropical Forest Science]] to develop a network of [[Forest Dynamic Plots]] that are surveyed regularly to sample the health of the forest. He won the [[Japan Prize]] for this in 2007.<ref>{{cite web |title=2007 (23rd) Japan Prize Laureate |url=http://www.japanprize.jp/prize/2007/e2_ashton.htm |publisher=www.japanprize.jp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070116212551/http://www.japanprize.jp/prize/2007/e2_ashton.htm |archive-date=16 January 2007}}</ref>

In 1983, Ashton was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web|title=Book of Members, 1780-2010: Chapter A|url=http://www.amacad.org/publications/BookofMembers/ChapterA.pdf|publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences|accessdate=25 April 2011}}</ref> He was elected Honorary Fellow of the Association for Tropical Biology and Conservation (ATBC) during the ATBC Annual meeting held in [[Kunming]], China, in 2006. In 2015 the ATBC created in his honor the Peter Ashton Prize, awarded annually to the outstanding article published in the journal ''[[Biotropica]]'' by a student. He was awarded the David Fairchild Medal for Plant Exploration in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fairchild Medal |url=https://ntbg.org/the-david-fairchild-medal-for-plant-exploration/ |access-date=2023-11-15 |website=National Tropical Botanical Garden |language=en-US}}</ref>
